items.title: Turn Any Photo Into Retro ASCII Art in Seconds
items.summary: Turn any photo into gloriously retro ASCII art — made entirely from letters, symbols, and tiny bits of chaos. This free tool turns your dog, face, logo, or worst holiday photo into something that belongs on a 1980s terminal. You will absolutely waste 10 minutes on it.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 011 – SpeedCurve’s INP Observer Missed Its Threshold
items.summary: A long-standing lux.js bug left Event Timing on its 104 ms default, while browser releases improve testing and rendering performance.

items.title: How the Prompt Box is Swallowing Website Interfaces Whole
items.summary: For decades, web designers obsessed over perfecting menus, tabs, and dropdowns. Now a single empty prompt box is quietly replacing them all. As AI turns websites into conversations, we're gaining incredible speed—but we may be losing something unexpected: the joy of discovery.

items.title: Canva Just Turned Affinity Into Adobe’s Biggest Free Problem
items.summary: Canva just made a much more serious play for professional designers: Affinity now brings design, photo editing, and layout into one free app, while Canva connects it to motion, AI, and team-friendly publishing tools.

items.title: Nobody Wants Your Damn App
items.summary: Nobody wants another app cluttering their phone—so why does every website keep begging us to install one? The web already perfected the experience: click, load, done. Maybe it’s time we stopped trying to ruin it.

items.summary: A wonderfully weird typeface from 1973 has come back to life — and somehow it looks more at home in 2026 than ever. Meet Clippy, the retro font that bends, rocks and wobbles its way into the digital age.

items.title: The Death of Apps Has Already Begun

items.title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up.
items.summary: AI can now build a UI in seconds, but that doesn't mean it built the UI you actually designed. A new Applitools integration turns Figma designs into visual baselines, automatically catching the subtle differences AI coding agents leave behind before they make it into production.
